interventions.agent: CNO (hM3Dq chemogenetic activation of LC-GABA neurons)

combinations.evidence_quote: We observed that yohimbine blocked the analgesic effects of chemogenetic activation of LC‐GABA neurons in both naïve and SNI mice (Figure S2D–G, Supporting Information).

combinations.readout: PWT and PWL on injured hind paw
combinations.magnitude: effect enhanced by simultaneous LC-NA activation
combinations.evidence_quote: In SNI mice, unilateral chemogenetic activation of LC‐GABA neurons increased PWT and PWL on the hind paw on the injured side, and this effect was enhanced by simultaneous optogenetic activation of LC‐NA neurons (Figure 5O,P).
While chemogenetic activation of LC‐GABA neurons alone mitigated depression‐like behavior in SNI mice, simultaneous activation of LC‐GABA and LC‐NA neurons exacerbated these behaviors (Figure 5U,V).

combinations.readout: mechanical PWT and thermal PWL (ipsilateral hind paw)
combinations.magnitude: analgesic effect less pronounced with LC-NA ablation
combinations.evidence_quote: CNO activation of LC‐GABA neurons increased PWT and PWL in both intact and ablation groups, although the analgesic effect was less pronounced in mice with ablation of LC‐NA neurons (Figure 6E,F).

combinations.readout: PWT, PWL, immobility time and CPP
combinations.magnitude: LC-GABA activation effects preserved with and without LC-NA ablation
combinations.evidence_quote: CNO activation of LC‐GABA neurons substantially elevated PWT and PWL, reduced immobility time, and established CPP in mice with and without LC NA neuron ablation (Figure 6M–T).

interventions.agent: optogenetic activation of LC GABA-vlPAG projection (ChR2)

combinations.magnitude: no further change versus vlPAG-GABA inhibition alone
combinations.evidence_quote: Combining CNO‐mediated inhibition of vlPAG‐GABA neurons with optogenetic activation of the LCGABA‐vlPAG pathway did not further alter PWT or PWL compared to chemogenetic inhibition of vlPAG‐GABA neurons alone.

interventions.agent: ChR2 activation of LC GABA-vlPAG pathway

combinations.magnitude: analgesic effect of LCGABA pathway activation blocked
combinations.evidence_quote: Similarly, a combination of CNO‐mediated vlPAG‐Glu inhibition with ChR2 activation of the LCGABA‐pathway did not produce any additional changes in PWT or PWL, although ChR2 activation of the LCGABA‐pathway alone significantly increased PWT and PWL (Figure S13O–R, Supporting Information).
